question:
Who said the following statement?

"We owe a lot to the Indians, who taught us how to count, without which no worthwhile scientific discovery could have been made!"
solution:
The correct answer is __**Albert Einstein**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Albert Einstein explained the phenomenon of the Photoelectric Effect.

__
 
• He won the Nobel Prize for the services in Theoretical Physics, with special regard to the discovery of the Photoelectric effect.
 
• The photoelectric effect is the phenomenon where when photons hit an electron on the metal surface, an electrical effect due to the release of electrons takes place.
 
• The wave-duality effect was discovered due to this very phenomenon.
 
• Max Plank discovered Energy Quanta (Nobel Prize in 1918)
 
• Neils Bohr - Atomic Structure and Quantum Theory (Nobel Prize in 1922)
 
• Ernest Rutherford - First who split the atom (Theory of Atomic Structure, Nobel Prize in 1908)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Frederick Herzberg**

 
 
• He has researched the issue of human motivation at work.
 
• Major works: 
 
 
• *Work and the Nature of Man (1966)*__
 
• __*The Motivation to Work (1959)*__
 
• __*The Managerial Choice: To be Efficient and to be Human (1976)*__
 
 
 
• Herzberg's motivation theory is based on the work experience of over 200 engineers. 
 
• The study's main goal was to see if different types of characteristics were responsible for job satisfaction. 
 
• In 1959, After the study, Frederick Herzberg proposed his Two Factor Theory or Hygiene or Motivation. 
 
 
 
• **Newton**
 
 
• Sir Isaac Newton described three laws of motion in his 1687 book Principia Mathematica Philosophiae Naturalis: 
 
• First law
 
• An object will remain at rest or in motion unless acted upon by another force.
 
• This law is also known as the law of inertia or Galileo's principle. 
 
• Second law
 
• The net force on an object is equal to the object's acceleration multiplied by its mass. 
 
• Third law
 
• If two objects exert forces on each other, the forces have the same magnitude but opposite directions. 
 
• Newton's laws of motion are used to describe the relationship between the motion of an object and the forces acting on it.
 
• They are used in many real-world applications, including simulating car collisions, navigating spacecraft, and playing basketball.
 
 
 
• **Galileo**
 
 
• A body moving with a certain speed along a straight path will continue to move at the same speed along the same straight path in the absence of the external field.
